It drifted closer to the South Pole, and the climate cooled, though flora remained.  After deglaciation during the latter half of the Early Permian, the land became dominated by glossopterids (an extinct group of seed plants with no close living relatives), most prominently Glossopteris, a tree interpreted as growing in waterlogged soils, which formed extensive coal deposits.  Other plants found in Antarctica during the Permian include Cordaitales, sphenopsids, ferns, and lycophytes.
